heading: INT. HOTEL LINEN ROOM - BASEMENT - NIGHT

units.text: INT. HOTEL LINEN ROOM - BASEMENT - NIGHT
A windowless cellar of steel shelves piled with folded sheets, bleached white.
Pipes sweat overhead.
A single bulb swings on its cord.
The air smells of starch and hot iron.
ABEL MORROW (50s, rumpled raincoat, a snub-nose revolver, a pocket recorder) enters sideways, back to the wall, eyes on the door he came through.
He shuts it with his heel.
He tests the handle.
Locked from the outside.
He presses RECORD.
The tiny reels turn.
Morrow. Basement linen room, Hotel Carnavon. Eleven forty. I'm alone.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: He walks the aisle between shelves, sliding the revolver along each row of towels as if one might hide a hand.
He checks the dryers, four huge steel drums, one by one, then crouches and looks under the folding table, then straightens with a grunt and a hand pressed to his ribs.
Somebody took a shot at me in the lobby. Whoever it was ran this way.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: A pipe knocks.
Abel freezes, revolver up.
Steam hisses from a valve and settles.
He exhales through his nose and lowers the gun.
He stops by a laundry cart, and lifts the top sheet, and lets it fall.
He picks up a white envelope from the cart.
His name is written across it in green ink.
He opens it with his thumb, reads, folds it, pockets it.
His jaw works.
Morrow. Basement linen room. Eleven forty-one. Found a note.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: He thumbs the recorder, rewinds a few seconds, and plays it back to himself.
Found a note.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: He nods to himself.
He clicks it forward again.
Note says it's from the night clerk. Says the clerk is dead, and I should stop looking for who killed him.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: He crosses to the shelves.
He drags a stack of towels aside, one at a time, and at the back there is a steel door, narrow, painted the same gray as the wall.
He puts his ear to it.
Silence.
He tries the handle.
Locked.
He steps back and fires twice into the lock.
The shots are enormous in the little room.
The bulb sways, flinging shadows, and the towels around him shiver.
The door sags open.
Behind it, a stairwell, narrow and dark, descending.
There's a stairway behind the shelf. I'm going down.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: He drops the recorder into his raincoat pocket without turning it off.
He ducks through the doorway and descends.
His footsteps echo away.
The bulb swings.
The recorder, still running inside the coat, whirs.
Morrow. Sub-basement. Twelve oh two. It's a church.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: Silence.
Then, far off, an organ begins to play.
Somebody's expecting me.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: The organ swells.
In the empty linen room, the swinging bulb catches a single white towel on the floor, unfolded, where there had been none.
